newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says aims to improve copper unit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says aims to improve copper unit.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Friday that it would put its full resources behind its copper division in an effort to improve its performance.

"In order to maximise shareholder wealth from our large copper business, actions have been put in place to bring to copper the full resources of BHP to expedite improved performance," BHP said in a statement accompanying its first quarter results.

BHP said for the balance of the 1996/97 financial year, 39 percent of its anticipated copper shipments were covered by put options at US$0.95 per pound and 10 percent by forward contracts at $1.07 per pound.
BHP's average price booked for copper shipments in the first quarter was $0.95 per pound down from $1.36 a year earlier.
BHP said unhedged copper shipments not finalised at August 31, 1996 have been brought to account at $0.92 per pound.
The group's copper division reported a 55.5 percent fall in profit to A$85 million for the three months to August 31.

Operations of the North American divisions were adversely affected by throughput and recovery problems at the Robinson mine in Nevada, low grades at the San Manuel and Pinto Valley mines in Arizona, BHP said.
It said the copper unit was also affected by high refining andf treatment charges at the Tintaya mine in Peru and the San Manuel smelter maintenance shutdown in August 1996.
